payload.feature:
One transcript law for every driver. The operator ruled in chat on 2026-09-02: "the same base implementation for claude, codex and dsh (and whatever else) — we always need the transcript."

Today each driver keeps its seat's transcript its own way. claude leaves it in ~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/<session>.jsonl and the journal records the session id; codex leaves it under its own home and the journal records the thread id (decision 0030); dsh keeps it under $DSH_HOME/sessions/brokkr/<seat>/ and the journal carries the path as the started checkpoint's clamped target (the retain ruling of run per-turn-checkpoints-for-the-dsh-d7ba1e44); exec keeps nothing. The ruling: every seat's transcript is the operator's, is always retained, and is addressable from the journal alone through one shape.

Enact:
1. One shape in the driver protocol, added the way the protocol's versioning law allows (contracts/ are frozen: a new version file, or a v1-compatible optional field if the loader's law permits that; say which in the decision and why): every driver reports a transcript in session_meta as {"kind": "claude-session" | "codex-thread" | "dsh-session" | "none", "locator": "<path or id, within the existing target clamp>", "home": "<the harness home it lives under>"}. Path or id only, never content: the journal's privacy invariant stands.
2. One base implementation in brokkr-protocol: a single transcript module every adapter arm calls. It resolves the harness home (claude: ~/.claude/projects; codex: $CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex; dsh: $DSH_HOME or ~/.dsh, reusing dsh_home and dsh_transcript_root_under as they stand), names the seat's transcript, and never deletes anything. Per-driver code supplies only the harness-specific locator; the shape, the clamp, the retention rule and the journal row are shared. exec reports kind none.
3. Surfaces: brokkr inspect's seat lines and the tui seat detail show the transcript under one plain label (0019 ruling 3), the same for every driver; where the locator is a claude session id the seat detail keeps the `claude --resume <id>` line it shows today. brokkr costs is unchanged.
4. A decision doc docs/decisions/0032-the-transcript-is-the-operators.md, Status: accepted (operator ruled in chat, 2026-09-02), citing run d7ba1e44's parked residual and its retry ruling as the evidence and stating the relation to the journal's privacy invariant: paths in, prose out. Index it in docs/decisions/README.md, and rewrite the transcript paragraph of docs/guides/driver-authoring.md to the shared shape.
5. Conformance: the driver conformance suite requires the transcript row from every built-in driver, with every shim harness pointed at a test home (DSH_HOME, CODEX_HOME, and the claude projects root injected the same way) so that no test ever writes under the operator's real homes.

Verification: cargo fmt --check, clippy, the full test suite, and the exact coverage gate at 100% lines, branches and functions. Windows CI: any path inside an sh -c script uses forward slashes and quotes, and every read is read -r.

result.notes: Implemented decision 0032 on current main: all built-in drivers now publish the shared retained transcript reference, inspect/TUI consume one label, Codex resume and export redaction use the common shape, and conformance isolates every harness home. cargo fmt --check, clippy, cargo test --workspace, and exact coverage all pass (14867/14867 lines, 2254/2254 branches, 1404/1404 functions). Changes are committed and not pushed.

Verifier seat, one run each, nothing changed. Step 1: `cargo test --workspace` from the worktree root at HEAD bec2805 on slice-transcript-law-2 (clean tree): every one of the 52 test-binary/doc-test result lines reads `test result: ok`; 915 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. Includes the machine proof (machine_proof.rs: 56 passed), the differential corpus parity tests (brokkr-core differential.rs: 3 passed), the driver conformance suite (driver_conformance.rs: 7 passed), frozen_contracts (2 passed), and the brokkr-protocol unit suite (85 passed) which carries the shared transcript module. Step 2: `cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self` compiled under the constitutional lint and emitted the full manifest (bundle digest b5e40fd0…2362, driver_protocol 1, database_schema 1, event_schema 1, engine 0.7.0, five seats intake/implement/verify/review/ship, every agent chain chosen at index 0 with no notices and nothing skipped). No error or lint output.

Reviewed the three run commits (18941f0, 31fe9ee, bec2805) against the 0032 framing on correctness, simplicity and security. Correctness: one transcript module in brokkr-protocol owns kind vocabulary, home resolution, 80-char clamp, session_meta insertion and the journal row; every adapter arm (claude/lanetally, codex, dsh, exec) calls it and supplies only its locator; finish() guarantees exactly one row per invocation including silent harnesses and exec's kind none; the engine's resume reads transcript.locator first and the flat session_id only as a pre-0032 fallback; the codex cold-fallback predicate is equivalent to the old contains_key check; the view validates the closed kind set, derives session_id only from claude-session locators for new journals, and bumps VIEW_VERSION to 5; inspect and the TUI render one plain `transcript` label and the TUI builds `claude --resume` only for a valid claude-session locator (provider-guarded for pre-0032 journals). Conformance injects HOME, CODEX_HOME and DSH_HOME as test-owned tempdirs, asserts one row per driver with the expected home, and the dsh root is still keep()'d with no remove_* call anywhere in adapters or transcript. No sh -c scripts were added, so the Windows path rule is untouched. contracts/ untouched; the decision correctly argues the nested optional field is v1-compatible because checkpoint data is an open object in driver-protocol.v1.schema.json. Security: the bridge's safe_checkpoint is allowlist-based, so the transcript object (including the operator's absolute home path) never leaves the journal, only session_reference_state=observed-redacted; the render surface wraps the cell in Safe and every TUI line goes through the one sanitizer; locators come from the child's pipe or a driver-created tempdir, never from the tailed dsh file; the dsh trust-boundary comment was updated accurately. Info only, no residual: (a) claude/codex invocations now fail closed when neither HOME nor USERPROFILE is set, which is the ruling's intent; (b) every claude/codex seat now journals the operator's absolute harness home, as the framing's `home` field requires, and the published journal anchor (0033) therefore carries it; the bridge withholds it. Fix applied and committed: docs/guides/driver-authoring.md claimed the bridge hashes locators; it withholds them and hashes only targets. Verified locally: cargo fmt --check clean, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo test --workspace all 52 suites ok.

Verified HEAD c14782a on a clean tree. Step 1: `cargo test --workspace` — 52 suites, every `test result: ok.`, 0 failed, 0 ignored; largest suites 223, 222, 85, 62, 56, 47, 43 passed; the machine proof, differential corpus parity, conformance and view suites all green, including the new transcript tests (the_transcript_shape_is_closed_and_its_absences_are_explicit, a_working_seat_carries_its_transcript_from_the_shared_checkpoint). Step 2: `cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self` — exit 0, no lint findings, emitted the manifest JSON (bundle self, digest b5e40fd0…, engine 0.7.0, driver_protocol 1, phases intake/implement/verify/review/ship/done/stop). Nothing changed, nothing committed.

Reviewed c14782a against pre-run 5100486 on all three dimensions; no file changed. Gates re-run here: cargo fmt --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings clean; instrumented workspace run (cargo +nightly llvm-cov, 45 suites ok) with LCOV evaluated by the gate script's rules: 0 uncovered DA records, 0 zero-taken and 0 dash BRDA records, LLVM function summary 1426/1426, no test source in the report. SECURITY (none): the transcript object is a whitelist casualty in the bridge (only session_reference_state leaves, test added); the locator is clamped to 80 and rendered only through Safe (inspect) and the tui span sanitizer; the claude --resume line is gated on kind == claude-session AND valid_session_id, so no codex/dsh locator can become a pasteable command; codex resume argv is still behind plain_thread_id; the shared module has no delete path; conformance injects HOME, CODEX_HOME and DSH_HOME so no shim writes under the operator's homes; the v1 contract declares checkpoint data as an open object, so the decision's 'v1-compatible additive field' claim holds. RESIDUALS: (1) low, correctness — crates/brokkr-cli/src/muninn.rs:487 usage() still reads session_id from the *-session-finished checkpoint; post-0032 session_meta carries transcript instead, so every new run's Muninn record now has session_id: null, and muninn/tests.rs fixtures still use the pre-0032 flat shape so nothing catches it. Not fixed here because the fix is a Muninn record-shape decision (add the transcript object vs. alias the locator), not a typo. (2) info — a real claude stream carries session_id in both system/init and result, so production claude seats will journal two transcript rows (record() re-publishes); harmless since view and engine take the last, but driver_conformance's 'exactly one common transcript row' holds only because the shim's result omits the id. (3) info — the claude/lanetally arm now refuses to start when neither HOME nor USERPROFILE is set (Transcript::resolve fails closed); previously it ran without a home. Fail-closed is the right direction but the decision doc does not state it.
